description: Low-frequency oscillator — six waveforms out at once: ramp down, ramp up, triangle, stepped random, square and sine

params.text: Calibrated in volts; 0V is C-3, 2.04Hz. V/OCT is added to it, seven octaves below a normal oscillator
Samples the output into a step function; the more it is turned up, the coarser the steps. CV at SAM
Pulse width of the square output. CV at PW
An offset added to the output, -5 to +5V, or 10 either way on the menu
Scales the output, before the offset is added
Smoothing: a slew limiter applied last of all, after offset and scale. It rounds the square into a shark fin and turns the stepped random output into a random walk

inputs.text: A 0-10V CV over the sampling, attenuated by the SAM knob
A bipolar CV, -5 to +5V, over the pulse width of the square output, attenuverted by the PW knob
One CV input shared by offset and smoothing; which of the two it drives is set on the menu
Pitch at a volt per octave, added to the frequency knob; the channels patched here set the polyphony
Hard sync, and it picks a new value on the stepped random output

outputs.text: A ramp rising from its trough to its peak over each cycle, a saw
A ramp falling from its peak to its trough over each cycle
A square, its width set by PW
A triangle, rising and falling in equal time
A new random value between -5V and +5V at each cycle, held until the next

menu: Offset range — sets what the OFFSET control covers, +/-5V or +/-10V
OFF/SM input routing — sends the CV at the shared jack To offset (OFF) or To smoothing (SM)
